summary: Chris Koerner and his business partner Brandon brainstorm ideas to make $10k in a year, month, week or day. Ideas include vibe-coded apps for die-hard hobby communities (board games, quilting, gardening), Chris's NEFL screener for founder-led network-effect stocks, local AI bootcamps with high-ticket upsells (Brandon has 27 sign-ups), shipping-container storage, luxury garage sales, buying estate-sale leftovers, and pop-up headshot booths. Chris also shows Backyard Fun House, a sport-court business that subs out every trade and gets leads from selfie-video Meta ads at $23-36 each, which he expects to turn $2,500 of ad spend into $25-45k net profit. Key takeaway: cheap AI-built apps and lead ads let you test ideas fast, and you should track ads through to closed deals.

ideas.name: Investment-thesis stock screener web app (NEFL)

tactics.name: Selfie-video Meta lead ads for home projects
steps: Record six unscripted selfie videos at the project site
Edit captions in CapCut (~5 minutes each)
Write headlines/primary text with ChatGPT
Run each ad in its own ad set at $100/day
Use a Meta instant form asking only name and phone
Push leads via Zapier to a Google Sheet with ad name
Score leads 1-10 and track close rate per ad; cut ads with high cost per lead

quote.text: my leads are pushing through to a Google Sheet through Zapier
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Pre-sell an event via newsletter form
steps: Add a Google Form to your newsletter announcing a $100 Saturday AI seminar
Collect topic and length preferences
Book a venue only once ~100 sign up
Plan seminar and upsells with ChatGPT

quote.text: I'll just have that link in my newsletter until I get to 100, and then that'll be the trigger
quote.speaker: Brandon

tactics.name: Back-of-room upsell tiers
steps: Low-cost seminar ticket covers ads/venue
Offer one-time ~$1k packages for small firms
Offer $2-3k/month 12-month contracts for larger firms
Offer a $10k shadow-for-a-day then automate offer
Brand locally ('Minneapolis AI Experts')

tactics.name: Niche community app ads
steps: Find large subreddits/Facebook groups for a passion hobby
Build a simple tracker app with AI coding
Run Reddit ads with a pain-point line that resonates

tactics.name: Use BATNA framing in buyouts
steps: Identify the seller's alternative (e.g. a $500 dumpster)
Offer a quick cash buyout that beats it
Promise to clear by morning

quote.text: So that's your that's your BATNA, your best alternative to a negotiated agreement
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Lease-option to de-risk a land business
steps: Lease land on a busy road for 12 months
Agree a purchase price upfront
Prove the model and line up investors/banks during the lease

lessons.lesson: Target die-hard hobby communities, especially in-person 'anti-AI' hobbies.

quote.text: It's simple and it has a very, very passionate audience

lessons.lesson: Side features can become the main product (Slack started as a game chat).
Any investment thesis can be productised as a web app.
Use a low-priced event to fund acquisition and profit on the high-ticket upsell.
Value-of-time arguments only hold if your time is fully optimised; doing it yourself can save $21k.

quote.text: It's just headaches plus 21,000 extra dollars

lessons.lesson: Track ad performance through to closes, not just cost per lead.

quote.text: I want to know which ads are are converting and to leads and which leads are converting to closes
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Pre-sell with a form before booking anything.
Buy others' 'sawdust': leftovers people would pay to dump.

evidence_quality.rationale: Mostly brainstormed hypothetical ideas; the sport-court ad results and newsletter sign-ups are first-hand but early and projected.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Beehiiv sponsor read and affiliate link; TK Owners; selling Fast Tree Care; promoting Backyard Fun USA.
